Short Course Description: This course discusses various uses of artificial intelligence in the Life Sciences industry and some of the ethical considerations one must consider when implementing such technologies.
Learning Objectives:
•	Identify current industrial applications of AI 
•	Identify industry opportunities and challenges
•	Understand responsible use of AI - safety, security, privacy, ethics and bias

Course: Introduction to Cybersecurity in Life Sciences
Short Course Description: This course explores the field of cybersecurity, and discusses the fundamentals of cybersecurity, best practices and common cyber threats.
Learning Objectives:
• Understand foundational concepts and areas of focus in relation to cybersecurity
• Identify best practices in cybersecurity
• Identify career opportunities and career paths in cybersecurity
• Understand popular and important resources related to the cybersecurity industry

Short Course Description: This course delves into the process of developing and manufacturing monoclonal antibodies (mAbs), covering different stages of development from drug discovery stage to formulation and filling.
Learning Objectives:
•	Understand the definition of biologics, its importance, and subcategories
•	Identify steps involved in the manufacturing process
•	Understand process development methodology
•	Gain an overview of the analytical techniques in mAB production
•	Understand the concept of quality by design
•	Career growth and opportunities

Short Course Description: This course provides an overview of different roles in various functional areas within the Life Sciences industry, such as Commercial, R&D, Regulatory Affairs, Market Access and Operations, and discusses practical steps towards starting a career in the Life Sciences industry.
Learning Objectives:
•	Understand the general organization structure of pharmaceutical companies
•	Identify roles, career path & key skills in different areas such as commercial, medical, R&D, regulatory, market access and government affairs

Short Course Description: In this course employees at Apotex discuss their work and career journeys. Walkthrough videos of R&D, Quality Operations and Manufacturing provide a behind-the-scene look at these departments.
Learning Objectives: •Understand how different departments function and what type of roles are available

Short Course Description: In this course employees at Eurofins Alphora discuss their work and career journeys, and provide a behind-the-scenes look at the R&D, Operations and Analytical Services departments.
Learning Objectives: •Understand how different departments function and what type of roles are available

Short Course Description: In this course employees at Microbix discuss their work and career journeys, and provide a behind-the-scenes look at roles in Quality Control, Manufacturing, R&D, Operations and more.
Learning Objectives: •Understand how different departments function and what type of roles are available

Course: Overview of the Canadian Life Sciences Industry (Life Sciences 101)
Short Course Description: This course provides a high-level overview of the Canadian Life Sciences landscape, covering topics such as product development cycle, regulatory review, pricing and reimbursement, intellectual property, sales and marketing and more.
Learning Objectives:
•	Identfy steps in the development cycle of life sciences products and typical timelines for each stage
•	Gain an understanding of regulatory processes and review 
•	Gain an understanding of the business side the life science industry

Short Course Description: This course provides an overview of the different forms of medical writing in the Life Sciences industry, and discusses the role of a medical writer and best practices.
Learning Objectives:
•	Differentiate between medical writing and scientific writing
•	Differentiate between regulatory writing and medical communications
•	Understand the role of medical writers, and skills and qualifications required
•	Understand the importance of Good Publication Practices.

Short Course Description: This course provides an overview of various stages of new vaccine and CMC development, from pre-clinical development to commercial manufacturing, and provides insights into the roles involved.
Learning Objectives:
•	Outline the process of developing new vaccines
•	Understand Chemistry Manufacturing and Control (CMC) development strategy at different phases (Phase I, Phase II, Phase III, etc)

Short Course Description: This course provides an overview of small molecule development, from drug discovery to API manufacturing processes to analytical and formulation development, and discusses various careers in this space.
Learning Objectives:
•	Identify what are small molecule medications 
•	Define terms such as Active Pharmaceutical Ingredients (API), Finished Dosage Forms (FDF), etc
•	Understand key elements of drug discovery and drug development, as well as drug product quality control and regulation

Short Course Description: This course discusses how business analytics is used throughout the value chain in the Life Sciences industry, and introduces concepts such as Competitive Intelligence (CI), Market Research (MR), strategic forecasting, market assessment, sales force effectiveness (SFE), incentive compensation (IC) and more.
Learning Objectives:
•	Understand how business analytics is applied across the value chain
•	Understand business terms such as competitive intelligence (CI) and market research (MR), basic and advanced strategic forecasting, market assessment and sizing, sales force effectiveness (SFE) and incentive compensation (IC)

Course: Essential Roles in Life Sciences Commercialization
Short Course Description: This course explores the sales, marketing and market access functions within the life sciences sector, with detailed discussion of potential career paths in life sciences commercialization.
Learning Objectives:
•	Understand Sales, Marketing and Market Access functions within the life sciences sector.
•	Identify potential career paths in life sciences commercialization

Short Course Description: This course explores the world of pharmaceutical sales, sales strategies and selling models, discussing the roles and responsibilities of a pharmaceutical sales representative and how the role is evolving.
Learning Objectives:
•	Identify the pharmaceutical product life cycle and stages
•	Understand the role and responsibilities of a pharmaceutical sales representative 
•	Appreciate the evolving landscape of pharmaceutical sales and future considerations

Short Course Description: This course explores the role of a product manager in the Life Sciences industry, and discusses strategies to engage key opinion leaders, price pharmaceutical products and establish a brand.
Learning Objectives:
•	Understand what is product management
•	Identify key functions in product management for life sciences sector

Short Course Description: This course highlights the roles and responsibilities of a project manager in the Life Sciences industry, and identifes different stakeholders and various strategy elements to ensure a product's success.
Learning Objectives:
•	Identify differences in drug development process for patented medicines versus generics
•	Understand the role of project managers

Course: Good Manufacturing Practices (GMP) for Quality Control
Short Course Description: This couse provides an overview of Good Manufacturing Practices (GMPs) in the context of quality control.
Learning Objectives:
•	Understand Good Manufacturing Practices (GMPs) in Quality Control
•	Understand how GMPs relate to Quality Control
•	Gain insights into relevant regulatory findings and observations in Quality Control

Short Course Description: This course discuses how Life Sciences companies interact with the government, the role of various government institutions and the different responsibilities of policy, regulatory affairs and market access teams in a Life Sciences company.
Learning Objectives:
•	Understand the relationship between the life sciences sector and the government
•	Understand the role of the main governmental institutions or organizations
•	Identify three key functional areas in which life science companies interact with public authorities
•	Describe the type of interactions with government representatives

Short Course Description: This course explores the various elements and goals of quality assurance in the life sciences industry.
Learning Objectives:
•	Gain a general understanding of how QC/QA is conducted 
•	Demonstrate basic understanding of environmental monitoring (EM)/sterility assurance
•	Demonstrate basic understanding of equipment/process qualification (Installation qualification (IQ), operational qualification (OQ), performance qualification (PQ))
•	Understand Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) writing and management, and biosafety standards through Public Health Agency Canada

Short Course Description: This course reviews the various cGXP guidelines in the pharmaceutical industry, and discusses the importance of quality management, drug establishment licensing, and the regulatory requirements of GCP, GLP, GDP, and GPP.
Learning Objectives:
•	Discuss the need for robust quality management systems 
•	Gain understanding of Drug Establishment Licensing requirements
•	Gain understanding of GxPs (GCP, GLP, GDP, GPP).

Short Course Description: This course explores the role of Regulatory Affairs team in life sciences companies, and discusses the regulatory approval process, from data collection to submission approval and post-market surveillance.
Learning Objectives:
•	Define what is Regulatory Affairs (RA) and the roles and responsibilities of regulatory agencies
•	Understand Canada-specific CMC requirements
•	Understand the concept of GMP (good manufacturing practices), and the importance of quality control and quality assurance 
•	Understand requirements for product labelling, pharmacovigilance and safety reporting

Short Course Description: This course provides a high-level general overview of the role of quality control testing and its importance in biopharmaceutical production. It discusses the complexity of biopharmaceuticals, potential process sampling points for testing and some of the key regulatory documents in quality control.
Learning Objectives:
•	Describe the importance of quality control testing 
•	Define the framework of basic testing requirements of a biopharmaceutical drug  
•	Provide an overview of some routine analytical test methods

Course: SUT: The Application of Single-Use Technologies in Biopharmaceutical Manufacturing
Short Course Description: The use of Single Use Technologies (SUT) in biopharmaceutical manufacturing has revolutionized the industry by providing flexibility, reducing cross-contamination, and decreasing capital and operating costs. This course provides a comprehensive understanding of the application of SUT in biopharmaceutical manufacturing.
Learning Objectives:
•	Define and describe what single-use technology and single-use systems are 
•	List advantages and risks associated with using single-use technologies 
•	Identify how single-use technologies are implemented throughout the upstream, harvest, and downstream bioprocess
•	Explain the future potential of single-use technologies in upstream and downstream processing 
•	List challenges that companies face when implementing single-use technologies

Short Course Description: This course provides an overview of the key concepts of cell therapy, the current state of manufacturing of these therapies and discusses how this may change in the future in order to meet the demands of a changing market.
Learning Objectives:
•	Define the concept of cell therapy
•	Discuss the difference between allogeneic and autologous therapies
•	Explain the manufacturing difficulties that currently exist
•	Discuss the various classes of therapy e.g. cellular immunotherapy and stem cell therapy
•	Describe how modification of cells is performed for therapeutic purposes
•	Understand how the industry may change to facilitate a growing market

Short Course Description: This course provides an overview of the key concepts of gene therapy and describes the various modification methods such as viral vector or nuclease delivery. It discusses current methods for scaling up the manufacture of these therapies and some ways in which this may be optimised in the future.
Learning Objectives:
•	Define the concept of gene therapy.To discuss the process by which genetic modification can alleviate disease
•	Explain the major classes of viral vectors that can be used to deliver gene therapies
•	List the typical manufacturing processes associated with viral vector manufacture
•	Discuss the concept of gene editing utilising nucleases
•	Understand the difficulties associated with some current manufacturing processes and how these may be optimised in future

Short Course Description: This course focuses on vaccine manufacturing in the context of various viral and bacterial vaccine production processes used in biopharma today. It provides a broad understanding of the complex and varied nature of vaccine manufacturing processes, while exploring specific details for particular vaccine types.
Learning Objectives:
•	Discuss the current demand for vaccines, the challenges in producing them, and the evolution of vaccine types throughout history. 
•	Understand common approaches to the manufacture of different vaccine types using a variety of starting materials
•	Understand new trends and technologies that will impact the future discovery, development, and manufacture of vaccines
•	Gain an insight into the research of vaccines for an increasing number of health concerns.

Short Course Description: This course looks at the current state of biopharmaceutical manufacturing and examine some of the drivers of change. It also discusses how methods and technologies, both in facility and equipment design, are facilitating manufacturing advances.
Learning Objectives:
•	Obtain an overview of some of the drivers of change in biopharmaceutical processing 
•	Receive a description of the technologies and concepts that are facilitating this change 
•	Gain an understanding of how facilities and processes may look in the coming years

Short Course Description: This course describes the different classes of cleanrooms. It also discusses potential contamination entry routes and do's and don'ts when working in a cleanroom with a focus on how personnel can reduce their contamination impact.
Learning Objectives:
•	Define the term 'cleanroom'
•	Describe the difference between controlled areas and critical areas 
•	Describe the types of contamination that can be found in a cleanroom 
•	Describe why people are the biggest source of contamination in a cleanroom
•	Explain the risk of contamination from personnel working in a cleanroom
•	List best practices when working in a cleanroom

Course: QRM Module 1: The Fundamentals of Effective Risk Management for Biopharmaceutical Manufacture
Short Course Description: This module defines what is meant by biopharmaceutical product risk and emphasizes the importance of examining risk through the lens of the patient. This course helps identify and classify different types of product and the importance of a proactive risk culture for patient safety.
Learning Objectives:
•	Understand the following “Knowing, Doing, Being” learning objectives 
•	Knowing: Understand what is meant by biopharmaceutical product risk, be able to explain the importance of examining risk through the lens of the patient
•	Doing: Be able to identify and classify different types of product risk. Be able to identify the key stakeholders and explain why the patient comes first
•	Being: Embrace the importance of a proactive risk culture

Course: QRM Module 2: Fundamentals of Risk Management
Short Course Description: This module builds awareness of the science and tools of risk management and discusses the potential impact of your behaviours on the reduction of risk to patients and the organization.
Learning Objectives:
•	Understand the following “Knowing, Doing, Being” learning objectives
•	Knowing: Gain clarity on the core Risk Management concepts.
Know the distinction between the management of risk and the assessment of risk. Understand the impact of human bias on decision-making
•	Doing: Be able to complete a risk ranking and a risk scoring exercise and perform rudimentary data analysis for estimating probabilities. Identify appropriate strategies to reduce the influence of bias on Risk Management outcomes
•	Being: Be OK with saying, “I don’t know the answer to that question”.
Be curious. Be transparent and brave when contributing to a Risk Management activity.

Course: QRM Module 3: Regulatory Requirements for Quality Risk Management in the Biopharmaceutical Industry
Short Course Description: The main focus of this module is to familiarize you with the key regulatory requirements, industry guidance and international standards associated with Risk Management and to make the connection to the underpinning current cGMPs. Armed with this knowledge you should feel confident to contribute to QRM activities.
Learning Objectives:
•	Understand the following “Knowing, Doing, Being” learning objectives
•	Knowing: Know the current Risk Management regulations for biopharmaceutical manufacture. Be aware of what the regulators are looking for in your Risk Management programs and practices. Understand the connection between the GMPs and Risk Management
•	Doing: Identify the core frameworks from the relevant regulations (e.g. ICH Q9, ISO 14971, WHO TRS 981). Distinguish between formal and informal risk management tools
•	Being: Practice the behaviors necessary to meet and exceed the minimum compliance requirements. Confidently contribute to risk management activities

Course: QRM Module 4: Implementing Effective Risk Control Strategies
Short Course Description: This module discusses the typical risk controls in place for products and processes in a biopharmaceutical manufacturing setting.
Learning Objectives:
•	Understand the following “Knowing, Doing, Being” learning objectives
•	Knowing: Be clear on what the “State of Control” means. Describe what a Product Control Strategy is. Gain further clarity about integration across the Risk Control Lifecycle
•	Doing: Actively engage in structured risk planning. Critically evaluate the effectiveness of current risk controls. Be able to access publicly available sources of risk control failures
•	Being: Be Confident. Be Curious. Communicate

Course: QRM Module 5: Application of Quality Risk Management Every Day
Short Course Description: This module reviews some examples of the everyday application of Risk Management.
Learning Objectives:
•	Understand the following “Knowing, Doing, Being” learning objectives
•	Knowing: Have an opportunity to review worked examples of everyday QRM examples. Participate in a Validation Risk Management Scenario
•	Doing: Be able to select appropriate actions or tools for a range of given risk events
•	Being: Describe the importance of involving individuals with a diverse range of skills and perspectives. Demonstrate the importance of maintaining vigilance and personal accountability

Short Course Description: This advanced course focuses on process development of ion exchange (IEX chromatography) in bioprocessing, including productivity and process economy of IEX and the the future of IEX.
Learning Objectives:
•	Understand separation principle and the role of pH, reasons for success, and challenges of IEX chromatography 
•	Discuss the versatility of IEX, with industrial application examples in downstream purification  
•	Discuss productivity and future of IEX in bioprocessing 
•	Identify the critical and key process parameters for optimization of IEX chromatography using high-throughput process development (HTPD) techniques

Short Course Description: This advanced course focuses on process development of mixed mode or multimodal (MM) chromatography in bioprocessing, and also discusses the economics and the future of this technology.
Learning Objectives:
•	Understand interaction principles, success factors, and challenges of MM chromatography 
•	Discuss industrial application examples of MM chromatography in downstream purification 
•	Discuss productivity and economic considerations of using MM chromatography in bioprocessing 
•	Identify the critical and key process parameters for optimization of MM chromatography using high-throughput process development (HTPD) techniques

Course: Overview of Host Cells for Bioprocessing
Short Course Description: This course reviews new therapy and drug formats with the potential to create a paradigm shift in the use of animal cell cultures, enabling you to select the right kind of host cell type for production of the protein of your interest.
Learning Objectives:
•	Describe the features and limitations of microbial, mammalian, insect and plant host cells 
•	Discuss factors to consider when selecting host cells for protein expression 
•	Understand current trends in the use of host cells

Short Course Description: This course explores in detail the operating parameters, their optimization and other key considerations for design and scale-up of an effective filtration process.
Learning Objectives: •	Understand key considerations for design and scale-up of an effective filtration process

Short Course Description: This provides an understanding of the underlying principles of good process design required to succeed in upstream biomanufacturing, discussing optimzation parameters to ensure robust cell growth.
Learning Objectives:
•	Understand underlying principles of good process design in upstream biomanufacturing
•	Understand the the concept of kinetic modeling 
•	Identify variables for bioreactor optimization
•	Discuss available methods and strategies to improve growth and limit cell death

Short Course Description: This course discusses how filtration works as a unit operation in the upstream and downstream stages of bioprocessing.
Learning Objectives:
•	Understand the mechanisms of action, classification of filters, process set-up, process parameters, maintenance, and applications for the different filtration modes
•	Identify the correct type of filter for your intended application

Short Course Description: This course identifies process capabilities needs in order to produce the required quality and quantity of biotherapeutics—with patient safety and drug effectiveness in focus. The course describes the role of quality by design as per ICH guidelines in bioprocess development.
Learning Objectives:
•	Understand the role of quality by design as per ICH guidelines in bioprocess development
•	Describe the different stages in biologics production 
•	Describe strategies used to prevent product and process-related impurities

Short Course Description: This course describes the operation of a mammalian cell culture bioreactor in the biopharmaceutical industry, critical parameters and the methods by which they are controlled. It also describes various modes of bioreactor operation and the advantages and disadvantages of each.
Learning Objectives:
•	Explain the fundamental design features of a mammalian cell culture bioreactor
•	Describe the critical parameters that may require control in a typical cell culture process
•	Describe the process considerations associated with cell culture scale-up using bioreactors
•	Discuss the effect of bioreactor control on other disparate parameters
•	Distinguish between batch, fed-batch and continuous modes of bioreactor operation

Course: Overview of the Biopharma Industry and Products
Short Course Description: This course describes the current healthcare landscape and role of biopharma industry, the dynamics of health around the globe and the various biotherapeutics available to treat both communicable and noncommunicable diseases. It describes different types of biotherapeutics used to fight disease, ranging from small molecules like insulin to large molecules like monoclonal antibodies, including some examples of blockbuster drugs.
Learning Objectives:
•	identify different types of biotherapeutics
•	recognize different drug development phases and the role of global and national regulatory agencies

Short Course Description: This intermediate-level course describe the principles of preparative chromatography for protein purification and how to perform it, covering performance factors including efficiency and resolution as well as throughput and productivity. This course also describes purification strategies and various modes of chromatographic operations and their practical applications and the methods used to scale up from a lab to production scale and relevant challenges.
Learning Objectives:
•	Familiarize yourself with different types of columns and stationary phases
•	understand types of chromatographic techniques like affinity and size exclusion chromatography. 
•

Course: Assessment and Certification for Fundamentals of Effective Risk Management
Short Course Description: Assessment module for QRM certification

Course: Module 6: Your Role in Preventing and Reducing Product and Patient Risk
Short Course Description: This module is designed to enable you to reflect on your learning across the course and to reinforce the importance of the role that you play everyday in preventing and reducing product and patient risk.
Learning Objectives:
Knowing
•	Understand that Risk Management is everyone's job.
Doing
•	Practice risk awareness and risk curiosity everyday.
Being
•	Demonstrate by your actions that you appreciate the fact that your individual actions may either uncover or contribute to a risk event.

Short Course Description: This prerequisite course for the GLP, GMP, QA/QC, and GCP courses introduces the various types of report writing required in bio-economy workplaces across Canada. It reviews the importance of written science communication skills, best practices and principles for writing reports, and the specific reports encountered in GLP, GMP, QA/QC, and GCP.
Learning Objectives:
"Learn to write scientific reports that contribute to:
•        Good Laboratory Practice (GLP)
•        Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP)
•        Good Clinical Practice (GCP)
•        Quality Assurance and Quality Control (QA/QC)
"

Short Course Description: This course defines and puts into practice GLP while demonstrating how to incorporate it into all laboratory procedures, how to complete a lab book, different ways to properly use equipment and materials, and the importance of following Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs).
Learning Objectives:
"Learn to apply GLP in your laboratory activities, including how to:
•        Complete a laboratory book
•        Use equipment
•        Use materials
•        Follow standard operating procedures (SOPs)
"

Short Course Description: This course defines and puts into practice GMP while demonstrating how to incorporate it throughout the manufacturing process by following SOPs, meet quality control requirements, run an investigation, and promote workplace health and safety.
Learning Objectives:
Learn to apply GMP throughout production, including how to:
•        Follow standard operating procedures (SOPs)
•        Meet quality control (QC) requirements
•        Run a successful investigation
•        Promote workplace health and safety

Short Course Description: This course defines and puts into practice QA /QC while demonstrating how they relate, how they differ and how they each apply, the importance of following SOPs; and key areas of health and safety and how to promote workplace health and safety.
Learning Objectives:
Learn to apply QA/QC in your workplace, including:
•        The differences between QA and QC
•        How to follow standard operating procedures (SOPs)
•        What a quality management system looks like
•        How to follow health and safety best practices

Short Course Description: This course defines and puts into practice GCP while demonstrating how to incorporate GCP into trials involving human subjects, how to protect the rights and safety of clinical trial subjects, how to ensure quality, integrity, and reliability of data gathered from trials, and how to follow GCP guidelines
Learning Objectives:
"Learn to apply GCP across all your research activities, including how to:
•        Align with the basics of GCP
•        Apply the basics of clinical research
•        Prepare and maintain required documents
•        Follow standard operating procedures (SOPs)
"

Course: Study Designs and Clinical Trial Phases
Short Course Description: This course introduces fundamental concepts and principles of clinical research, focusing on the different study designs and clinical trial phases. The foundational information provided in the course allows a better understanding of health-related improvements to which both clinical research, and more specifically clinical trials, have contributed.
Learning Objectives:
•	Identify the importance of clinical research, clinical trials, and standard of care in the context of health care.
•	Identify the different types of clinical trial designs and the key features to consider when designing and conducting trials.
•	Identify the characteristics of the pre-clinical stage and clinical trial phases.

Short Course Description: This course introduces the fundamental concepts and principles that pertain to the drug discovery and development process. Before a drug is tested in a clinical trial, there is a need to: identify a medical problem, discover and develop a drug, understand if the drug works and how, and decide whether it is safe to test it in humans. This course summarizes the process underlying drug discovery and development, leading to an investigational product being tested in clinical trials.
Learning Objectives:
•	Identify the major milestones in the history of drug discovery and development.
•	Identify the different types of therapeutic compounds.
•	Identify stages of the drug discovery and development process.
•	Identify challenges of drug discovery and development.

Short Course Description: Free and informed consent is a founding principle of research ethics. Patients must fully understand and freely choose to participate in a research study. Informed consent protects the rights of the patient /participant and builds trust between the participant and the study team. This course will explain the informed consent process and the ethical principles behind it.
Learning Objectives:
•	To identify the purpose and principles of informed consent
•	To identify the essential elements of the consent process
•	To identify special circumstances in informed consent.

Short Course Description: Research participants are vital to the success of clinical research and volunteer their time to be part of a study, so the process of recruitment requires a patient-centric approach that respects their contribution. By the end of this course, learners will be able to understand the basic concepts and guidelines around recruiting participants and the importance of keeping them engaged throughout the study.
Learning Objectives:
•	To identify the process for recruiting the target population of the study
•	To identify participant recruitment strategies and considerations
•	To identify approaches to enhance participant engagement and retention

Short Course Description: Adverse Events (AEs) encompass any unfavourable or undesirable medical occurrences that were not observed prior to an individual's participation in research, including the worsening of existing symptoms, regardless of whether they were expected or attributed to the study. This course delves into fundamental concepts surrounding AE management, crucial for ensuring participant safety in clinical research. It covers how AEs are detected, assessed, and classified and offers guidance on AE reporting.
Learning Objectives:
•	To identify how participant safety is maintained through adverse event monitoring
•	To identify the methods for detecting, assessing and classifying adverse events
•	To identify the guidance surrounding adverse event reporting in clinical trials

Short Course Description: This course is designed to provide learners with an introductory understanding of clinical study oversight and monitoring and its significance in maintaining participant safety, data integrity and regulatory compliance. This course also familiarizes learners with the different types of monitoring visits, along with the oversight responsibilities of the various persons and groups involved in a clinical trial.
Learning Objectives:
•	To identify the importance of study oversight and monitoring in clinical trials
•	To identify the roles and responsibilities in study oversight and monitoring
•	To identify the different types of monitoring visits and their purpose

Short Course Description: This course presents the management of data in the context of clinical research throughout the entire research data life cycle, from study start-up to study closure. The various types of media and documents containing or holding research data are explored in this context. This course also delves into best practices and requirements for data access, sharing, security, storage, and privacy, emphasizing their importance in maintaining data integrity in clinical research.
Learning Objectives:
•	To identify general concepts regarding data management in the context of clinical research
•	To identify steps in the clinical data management process
•	To identify data privacy and storage requirements in clinical research

Short Course Description: The protocol acts as a guidebook for a clinical trial and details each part of the study, how it should be carried out, and by whom. This course introduces the key sections of a standard clinical trial protocol and what should be included in each. It also highlights the importance of clinical trial protocols and their implications for participant safety.
Learning Objectives:
•	The importance of the clinical trial protocol
•	The sections and characteristics of a well-designed clinical trial protocol
•	Important considerations related to clinical trial protocols.

Course: Role and Responsibilities in Clinical Research
Short Course Description: Clinical research involves multiple teams of people with a variety of skills and experience, working together to develop, coordinate and test innovative treatments or interventions while protecting the safety, well-being and rights of research participants. This course explains who is involved in clinical research, as well as their roles and responsibilities and how, from a general perspective, research teams are organized at sites.
Learning Objectives:
•	To identify key players in the governance and conduct of clinical trials
•	To identify the roles and responsibilities of the site clinical investigation team
•	To identify the concepts of task delegation and scope of practice

Short Course Description: Study records contribute to overall study data and provide documented evidence of study assessments. Good Documentation Practices (GDP) are critical to collecting and recording sound research data and complying with regulatory requirements. This course provides an overview of the principles of Good Documentation Practices, including the ALCOA+ principles, and their importance in ensuring data integrity and quality.
Learning Objectives:
•	To identify Good Documentation Practices and their rationale
•	To identify the ALCOA+ principles
•	To identify best practices for recording data in clinical trial setting

Short Course Description: Patient engagement in research is key to improving the relevance and quality of clinical research, increasing patient trust and satisfaction, and ultimately, improving health outcomes. By the end of the course, learners will be familiar with key concepts and guiding principles of patient engagement.
Learning Objectives:
•	Identify the foundational concepts underlying patient engagement in research
•	Identify guiding principles and implications for engaging patients in research
•	Identify the importance of fostering patient engagement in research despite barriers

Course: ICH Guidance E6(R2) GCP (International Council for Harmonisation-Good Clinical Practice)
Short Course Description: This course is designed for clinical research professionals, trainees in health sciences, and community partners who are, or will be, engaged in research involving humans.
Learning Objectives:
•	To identify the principles of GCP in the conduct of research involving humans. 
•	To recognize the roles and responsibilities of the investigator, sponsor, research ethics board, and research team members before, during, and after study. 
•	To recognize key best practises in clinical research and some of the common tools to help achieve compliance.

Course: Health Canada, Part C, Division 5 of the Food and Drug Regulations
Short Course Description: The Food and Drug Regulations are the federal requirements for the sale and importation of drugs used in human clinical trials in Canada. This course introduces the regulatory process and key requirements such as clinical trial applications, amendments, good clinical practice, reporting, and ending a clinical trial early. Upon completing this course, scientists, clinical research professionals, patient partners, and trainees will understand how to include regulatory requirements into clinical research.
Learning Objectives:
•	Identify the regulatory process for authorization of the use of drugs in human clinical trials, including applications and amendments. 
•	Identify the sponsors responsibilities in terms of good clinical practise. 
•	Recognize the requirements for the proper handling of drugs, including labels, records, and storage. 
•	Identify the process for reporting serious unexpected adverse drug reactions during a clinical trial.
•	Identify the process for ending a clinical trial early, including by the sponsor or health Canada.

Course: Tri-Council Policy Statement-Ethical Conduct for Research Involving Humans TCPS 2 (2022)
Short Course Description: This course introduces learners to ethics-related issues that may arise in research involving human participants, including their data and/or biological materials.
Learning Objectives:
•	Recognize the importance and role played by the tri-council policy statement (TCPS 2) as a set of ethical guidelines for research involving human participants. 
•	Identify the three core principles on which TCPS 2 is based and their appropriate application depending on the context. 
•	Recognize the specificities of monitoring and management of ethics review processes in research. 
•	Identify the principles for ethically managing conflict of interest. 
•	Recognize the ethical and operational approach for research involving indigenous peoples.

Short Course Description: This 5 day in-person bootcamp is part of OBIO/CATTI’s Biomanufacturing for Advanced Therapies Training Program, focusing on both conceptual and practical skills essential for the rapidly growing field of Advanced Therapy Medicinal Products (ATMPs). This one-week (~40 hrs), hands-on training bootcamp at CATTI’s Guelph facility (on-site) is designed for participants to master key skills such as cell culture, aseptic techniques, and good documentation practices in a GMP-simulated setting, with proficiency assessed by experienced trainers. Online prerequisites: lab safety, introduction to ATMP industry, Advanced Therapies GMP onboarding learning path
This bootcamp is geared towards early stage startup. Online prerequisites: OBIO business development learning path

In this course, we provide an accelerated introduction to the core competencies of data science using R. We start with an introduction to R's computing environment and workflow for conducting complex and reproducible analyses. We introduce efficient methods for data wrangling, import/export, cleaning, and processing relevant to both industry and academic data scientists. A formal framework for data visualization is presented through a grammar of graphics common to many data science languages. We conclude with lessons on written and oral data story telling for both industry and academia. Blended format: 2 days online (synchronous) + 3 days in person. Offered once per year.
Learning Objectives:
•	Apply their foundational understanding of how data is processed in R to write efficient, neat, and reproducible analysis scripts. 
•	Perform data import and pre-processing of raw, messy data from a variety of sources. 
•	Apply ‘grammar of graphics’ principles to create insightful data visualizations. 
•	Tell a cohesive story with their data using visualization.
Format: Blended (2 days online synchronous + 3 days in person)

Short Course Description:
: In this course, we will examine emerging data privacy and security challenges in the age of AI and machine learning. We develop research skills to identify and analyze current privacy and security threats, real-world case studies, and their impacts. 
We will introduce key concepts and demonstrations of AI-driven security and privacy risks and fundamental defense mechanisms. An introduction to fundamental concepts in data governance and ethical considerations in cybersecurity will be provided. 
Through short literature reviews, presentations, in-class demonstrations, and hands-on practice, you will be equipped with common strategies to assess and mitigate modern threats in various domains. By the end of the week, you will develop a solid understanding of AI’s role in data privacy and security.  Blended format: 2 days online (synchronous) + 3 days in person. Offered once per year
Learning Objectives:
•	Investigate recent data privacy and security threats in their own fields.  
•	Apply common data privacy-protection solutions to reduce privacy and security risks.  
•	Examine the use of AI and Machine Learning in data privacy and security.  
•	Analyze the principles of data governance in cybersecurity
Format: Blended (2 days online synchronous + 3 days in person)

Course: Bootcamp - Principles and Practices of Biorisk Management
Short Course Description:
The Principles and Practices of Biorisk Management course is a comprehensive five-day professional development program designed for biosafety officers, institutional biosafety committee members, laboratory managers, and research professionals responsible for biosafety, biosecurity, and compliance. This in-person training provides the essential knowledge and practical tools necessary to implement effective biorisk management systems aligned with Canadian and international regulatory requirements.
Participants will engage with experts from academia, government, and the biosafety community to explore both foundational and advanced topics, including:
• Biosafety and biosecurity risk assessments
• Emerging technologies such as CRISPR, viral vectors, and self-driving labs
• Integration of biosafety with engineering controls and infrastructure design
• Emergency preparedness, medical surveillance, and inspection planning
• Regulatory compliance with the Human Pathogens and Toxins Act (HPTA) and Public Health Agency of Canada (PHAC)
Through case studies, interactive sessions, and practical exercises, attendees will gain actionable skills to enhance institutional biosafety programs and prepare for inspections, audits, and emergency scenarios.

Course: Introduction to Pharmaceutical Regulatory Affairs (full course)
Short Course Description: This online (synchronous) course describes the role of the Regulatory Affairs department in a pharmaceutical organization and focuses on the submission process and the legal requirements that control the process for pharmaceuticals, natural health products and medical devices.  The regulatory requirements at the various stages in drug product development from inception through market authorization are examined. Assignments on label development, drug and establishment licenses, regulatory submission planning and responses, medical device classification and post-NOC documentation provide participants with practical experience in developing regulatory documents and strategy.
Learning Objectives:
•	Describe the role of the Regulatory Affairs department in a pharmaceutical firm, its relationship to other departments in the firm and to external regulatory bodies.
•	Describe the development stages of a drug product or medical device and the corresponding legislated submission requirements.
•	Implement those sections of the drug legislation in which the Regulatory Affairs department is routinely involved, for example: recall, complaint handling and ADRs, SOPs, regulatory inspections, and deficiency correction.
•	Describe current legislation for patents, trademarks and copyrights and how it affects the submission approval process.
•	Characterize Post-NOC Changes and SU/PAC Changes based on the requirements of Health Canada (HC) and the Food and Drug Administration (FDA).
•	Prepare an acceptable submission for a DINA Application in Non-eCTD Electronic format and Establishment Licence (EL).
•	Apply the various sections of a drug submission and the regulatory requirements related to them in preparing requisite forms and communications.
•	Compare the submission requirements for a Natural Health Product with classical pharmaceutical applications.
•	Explain the Canadian and U.S. submission filing requirements for a Medical Device.
